top3.headline: Trump threatens a 'tremendous tax' on data centers built abroad
top3.whyItMatters: Where you build AI capacity is now a political choice, not just a cost decision.

top3.headline: METR: AI keeps improving fast, but judgment still trails coding
top3.whyItMatters: Hand agents coding-like tasks first and keep judgment calls with your people.

top3.headline: OpenAI moves to stop others copying its models via distillation
top3.whyItMatters: Copied models may ship without safeguards, so know where your AI really comes from.

items.title: Perplexity Computer now takes delegated tasks inside Chrome
items.takeaway: Aravind Srinivas says you can now delegate tasks to Perplexity Computer on Chrome.
items.soWhat: Agents are moving into the browser your team already uses every day.

items.title: Lyn Alden: bonds flat since Nov 2 while stocks, gold, bitcoin fell
items.takeaway: She notes bonds have been basically flat since November 2 while stocks, gold and bitcoin all fell.
items.soWhat: A quick read on where money is holding up as risk assets slide.

items.title: Theo calls Gemini 4 Neon an incredible model
items.takeaway: Theo says Gemini 4 Neon is an incredible model, one more builder reaction since its launch this week.
items.soWhat: Builder praise is an early signal of which model your developers will ask for next.

items.title: Isomorphic Labs partners with Merck to design a new cancer drug
items.takeaway: Demis Hassabis announces the collaboration and calls it a proof point for Isomorphic's reimagining of drug discovery.
items.soWhat: AI drug design is moving from funding rounds to deals with big pharma.

items.title: OpenAI details how it detects and disrupts model distillation
items.takeaway: OpenAI says distillation can reproduce powerful capabilities without their safeguards, and describes how it spots and disrupts coordinated attempts.
items.soWhat: Copied models can arrive without safety guardrails, a new risk for anyone buying AI.

items.title: OpenAI launches MedChemBench to test AI on drug chemistry
items.takeaway: OpenAI says the new benchmark shows frontier models improving at helping scientists identify promising drug candidates.
items.soWhat: Labs now measure AI against scientific work, not just chat and code.

items.title: Trump threatens a 'tremendous tax' on data centers built abroad
items.takeaway: Trump said: 'We're not going to allow our companies to build data centers outside of our country', The Verge reports.
items.soWhat: Plans to build AI capacity outside the US could face new costs and political risk.

items.title: METR update: AI keeps improving fast, but judgment lags coding
items.takeaway: MIT Technology Review covers METR's new report: some capabilities still grow exponentially, while judgment tasks trail coding.
items.soWhat: Delegate coding-like work first; keep judgment calls with people for now.

items.title: Anthropic mathematician claims a Riemann proof with Claude, unverified
items.takeaway: Levent Alpöge says he and Claude found a proof and formalized the arguments; The Verge notes it is not yet verified.
items.soWhat: If verified, AI becomes a partner on the hardest problems, not just an assistant.

items.title: Ray Dalio: failure comes with being adventurous
items.takeaway: He recalls a market mistake in which he lost everything and had to borrow money to cover family expenses.
items.soWhat: Taking big bets means planning to survive the misses, not avoiding them.

items.title: Signal blocks screenshots so OS-level AI agents can't read chats
items.takeaway: The Verge says Signal now restricts screenshots on Android and iOS to keep agents like Gemini and Siri off on-screen data.
items.soWhat: Apps are starting to wall off agents; check what your own tools let them see.

items.title: Ruben Hassid: 20 minutes to set Claude up for 7 business jobs
items.takeaway: He says to go beyond rewriting emails, starting with Claude for small business; any paid plan works.
items.soWhat: A short setup can turn a chat subscription into real help across the business.

items.title: Anthropic says Claude solved two open problems in black-hole physics
items.takeaway: Anthropic's research post, on the Hacker News front page, says Claude solved two open problems in the physics of black holes.
items.soWhat: A second science claim in a day suggests labs will compete on discovery.

items.title: Anthropic's Nasdaq debut puts AI's promise to a Wall Street test
items.takeaway: Reuters frames the debut as a test of AI's promise and peril; Gary Marcus argues the stock is already crashing.
items.soWhat: Public markets will now grade frontier labs daily, and sentiment can turn fast.

voices.quote: I believe I have, working with Claude, discovered a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis

hotOnX.text: NVIDIA has to become a frontier lab faster than frontier labs are becoming chip companies.
hotOnX.note: A sharp line on chip makers and AI labs racing into each other's business.

hotOnX.text: Somewhere Euler, Gauss and Riemann in awe today!
hotOnX.note: Google's CEO marks a big day for AI and math.

hotOnX.text: The story so far, told by Anthropic's seven co-founders.
hotOnX.note: Interest in Anthropic stays high in its first days as a public company.

hotOnX.text: Prompt of the day: review every code comment in a codebase and categorise each, e.g. Tautology or Excuse.
hotOnX.note: A copyable prompt that stops agents hiding hacks behind comments.

hotOnX.text: Introducing MedChemBench, a new benchmark for AI reasoning in medicinal chemistry.
hotOnX.note: Drug discovery is becoming a headline test for frontier models.
